family: ONE THING FOUND OUT BY THE HAND GOING INTO A SPACE NO EYE CAN SEE INTO, AND NOTHING CHANGED. A hand, or part of one, goes into a space no eye can get to — behind a thing, into a gap between two things, down a bore or a slot, into a hollow in the ground, into a crack round a cast thing, under the far side of a thing — and the whole of what the chapter knows at the end is how far in the hand goes, what is at the far end of it, what the thing is resting on, or how much it gives. The object is only the reason the hand went there. Nothing marked, cut, fastened, filled, shimmed, written down, put right, and no second pair of hands on the thing in hand.
why_not_the_nearest: 0065 WAS ONE SHALLOW FIX ON TIRED GROUND WITH A TOOL. 0066 WAS ONE SHALLOW KEEP ON GROUND ALREADY MOVED WITH A TOOL. 0067 WAS ONE LOOSE THING TAKEN IN HAND, LOOKED AT, AND PUT DOWN AGAIN, THE WHOLE OF ITS FINDING MADE BY LOOKING. 0068 WAS ONE THING MEASURED WITH THE HAND USED AS A GAUGE AGAINST AN EXPOSED FACE, SO THE ANSWER CAME OFF THE OUTSIDE OF THE THING IN THE OPEN AIR. HERE THE ANSWER CAME FROM INSIDE A CLOSURE, EVERY TIME, AND THE GAUGE AND THE PROBE ARE NOT THE SAME INSTRUMENT.

ten_gestures_and_the_rule_about_them: THE GESTURE IS THE ACTION OF THE HAND AND NOT THE OBJECT, AND NO TWO CHAPTERS MAY USE THE SAME GESTURE. THIRTY HANDS ARE SPENT IN 855 TO 884 AND NONE OF THEM APPEARS HERE. THE FIVE OBJECT-MANIPULATION GESTURES LEFT UNSPENT ON THE 0067 MENU — ROLLED BETWEEN FINGER AND THUMB, BALANCED ACROSS TWO FINGERS AND TIPPED, PINCHED OFF BETWEEN THUMBNAIL AND NAIL, SQUEEZED ONCE, SET DOWN AND PICKED UP BY A DIFFERENT PART — ARE BANNED HERE AS THEY STAND, BECAUSE EVERY ONE OF THEM IS A HAND ACTING ON A THING ALREADY IN THE HAND AND NOT ONE OF THEM PUTS A HAND INTO A CLOSURE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF THIS FAMILY. THE TEN BELOW ARE THE EIGHT FREE HANDS ON THE 0070 PROMPT LIST PLUS TWO WRITTEN FOR THIS BLOCK, AND EVERY ONE IS A HAND THAT GOES SOMEWHERE AND DOES NOT COME BACK WITH THE THING.

cards.0885: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a five-bar gate across the front of her yard with a stub of sandstone stood on end in the ground behind its leading edge as a stop, and means to put the thumb of one hand into the hollow behind that leading edge and leave it there while the fingers of the same hand walk down the face of the stile, and to find out where the gate is against the stop and where it is not. The stop is never moved, the gate is never lifted off its hinges, the long piece of stone lying flat in the ground behind the stub is not dug up, no joint is pointed and no room is entered.
cards.0886: At the unit a man in his early forties has a length of four-inch cast iron pipe stood on end in the corner at the gate end of that yard with its socket uppermost, and means to put one hand down flat into that socket palm to the ground and then turn the forearm on its edge after the hand and drive the arm down as far as the shoulder will lift it, one inch past the place where the arm wants to stop, and to find out what the bore of that pipe does on its way down. The pipe is not lifted, nothing is taken out of it, no water is drawn and no bar goes into it. The latch stays hooked, the staple is NOT DONE and April is NOT PAGE.
cards.0887: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a boundary wall along the front of her garden with a coping of long stones bedded on it, and means to lay one hand along the joint where two of those coping stones meet with the nails turned down and following the joint the whole way, and to find out how deep that joint is and what is at the bottom of it. No coping stone is lifted, no joint is pointed, no mortar is put anywhere, the gate is not touched, the wedges are not moved, the spanner is not picked and the coal is not opened.
cards.0888: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a length of pipe stood on end in the corner of that yard with nails in it, and means to put one hand down inside that pipe and then close the other hand round the wrist of the first and push, so that the force comes out of the arm and not out of the fingers, and to find out what is standing in the bottom of it. The pipe is not lifted, no nail is taken out and nothing is shaken. The heap of broken base is not touched, the square hole gets nothing put in it, the oval holes are not filled or plugged and the kerb is not set square to.
cards.0889: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a cold frame standing at the end of a bed with no glass in it since November, and means to lay one hand flat on the soil of that bed and push it forward until it stops, and to find out what stops it. The frame is not lifted, nothing is put under it, no glass goes in, the tap is not touched, no water is drawn, the line is not put right, and the drawer is neither opened nor shut.
cards.0890: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a shed standing at the far end of that yard with its side a foot clear of the boundary wall at the gate end, and means to put one hand into that slot at the gate end and the other into it at the far end and work them towards each other until they meet, and to find out what joins the two walls in the middle and what they are both standing on. Nothing is put into the slot, nothing is taken out of it, the three courses of brick that join the walls are not touched, no wall is rebuilt, the heap is not taken down and no room is entered.
cards.0891: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has an ivy growing up the wall of the shed at the end of the bed, and means to put one hand down into the hollow where the stem leaves the ground and turn it palm up under the arch the stem makes there, and to find out where the stem has actually gone. The slab is not lifted, nothing is cut, the ivy is not pulled off the wall, the felt and the ply are neither touched nor nailed, the thread is not cut and the line is not put right.
cards.0892: At the unit a man in his early forties has a cast drain frame set into the concrete at the wall end of that yard, and means to walk the fingers of one hand into the crack round that frame a finger at a time until a finger will not go, and to find out how deep into the concrete the frame has been let. No concrete is cut, no grout is put down anywhere, the frame is not lifted and no bar goes into it. The latch stays hooked, the staple is NOT DONE and April is NOT PAGE.
cards.0893: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has two pallets lying in the corner of that yard, one on the other and not square to each other, and means to put one hand in flat under the far side of the upper pallet and push it along under it until the arm stops, and to find out what the upper pallet is standing on. No pallet is lifted, nothing is put under either of them, the pipe of nails is not touched, the shutter stays down and not out of its guides, the bench is not moved, and the oval holes are not filled or plugged.
cards.0894: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a front door with a keep on the edge of it standing proud of the face of the door, and means to turn one hand on its edge and push it into the gap beside that door, the back of it leading, and to walk it down the whole height of the gap, and to find out what is in that gap for the length of it. The door is not taken off, the keep is not planed and no oil goes anywhere. The gate is not touched, the turf is not laid back down and the coal is not opened.

review_pass_findings: 0887 HAD 0889'S DATE. THE DATELINE READ THURSDAY THE TWENTY-NINTH OF FEBRUARY 2024 INSTEAD OF THE TWENTY-SECOND, WHICH PUT TWO CHAPTERS ON ONE DAY, PUT A TEN-DAY GAP IN WHERE THE PLAN HAS FOUR, AND RAN THE WHOLE SEQUENCE BACKWARDS FROM 0887 TO 0888. CORRECTED.

0885'S STONE ARITHMETIC DID NOT CLOSE. A STUB EIGHTEEN INCHES HIGH PLUS TWO FEET LYING FLAT IS THREE AND A HALF FEET AND NOT THE TWO AND A HALF THE CHAPTER SAID. THE WHOLE LENGTH IS NOW THREE AND A HALF FEET.

0885'S CENTRAL FINDING COULD NOT BE PRODUCED BY THE OBJECT. THE ORIGINAL HAD THE GAP OPEN ABOVE AND BELOW A SINGLE STONE, WHICH ONE STONE ON END CANNOT DO. THE FINDING IS NOW TWO ZONES: A FINGER'S WIDTH OPEN AT THE TOP FOR THE LAST FEW INCHES OF A TWO-FOOT LEADING EDGE, AND CLOSED FROM THERE TO THE GROUND, WITH A GATE SHUTTING ON THE LOWER THREE PARTS OF FOUR OF ITS HEIGHT.

0885'S WEAR EVIDENCE DID NOT FOLLOW FROM ITS OWN GEOMETRY. A GATE THAT MUST BE LIFTED BODILY OVER AN EIGHTEEN-INCH STOP DOES NOT GRIND A HOLLOW IN THE GROUND WITH ITS FOOT. THE HOLLOW IS GONE AND THE EVIDENCE IS THE SOIL HAVING COME UP ROUND THE STONE AND THE THINNER GRASS OVER IT.

0886 HAD THE HAND COMING OUT OF THE BOTTOM OF A PIPE THAT WAS STANDING ON THE FLAGS, AND THEN SAID THE BORE WAS CLEAR AND THEN SAID THERE WAS AN INCH OF GRIT IN IT. THE HAND NOW STOPS AT THE BOTTOM OF THE PIPE AND FINDS THE GRIT AND, THROUGH THE GRIT, THE RIDGE OF A FLAG JOINT RUNNING UNDER IT.

0886 NESTED TWO FOUR-INCH PIPES, WHICH IS NOT POSSIBLE. THE OUTER IS FOUR-INCH AND THE INNER IS A THREE-INCH LENGTH, AND WHAT THE HAND FEELS IS ITS THREE-AND-A-QUARTER SPIGOT STOPPED BY THE SHOULDER OF THE OUTER SOCKET. THE ANNULAR GAP IS THREE-QUARTERS OF AN INCH AND NOT A QUARTER.

0887'S JOINT DEPTH DID NOT CLOSE AND THE CHOCK WAS NEVER LOCATED. THE JOINT IS FIVE INCHES DEEP WITH CEMENT FROM ONE INCH DOWN TO THREE INCHES DOWN AND THE CHOCK LYING FLAT IN THE BOTTOM INCH AND A HALF, AND THE THING THE NAIL COMES ON AT THREE AND A HALF INCHES IS THE TOP OF THE CHOCK.

0888'S BATTEN DID NOT FIT ITS OWN BORE. A THREE-INCH BATTEN WITH THREE INCHES OF NAILS ABOVE IT DOES NOT GO IN FOUR INCHES. THE BATTEN IS AN INCH AND A HALF THROUGH WITH AN INCH AND A HALF OF NAILS ABOVE IT.
